judgments.reasoning_cat1: The words and numerals disagree on their face: "Three Million ($1,000,000) dollars aggregate" is a mechanical error that changes the amount required, and "occurrence basis, or claims made including tail coverage" leaves the choice and duration of tail coverage undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 9 cross-refers to "the insurance coverage set forth in section 8" without repeating any figure, so nothing elsewhere in the MTA resolves the words/numerals mismatch, but nor does anything contradict the obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow, mechanical certificate-of-insurance obligation triggered "upon request"; the two limbs are definite and the only obscurity is OCR damage to the romanettes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cross-reference to section 8 is accurate and consistent with the numbering, unlike the survival clause's reference to "Sections 5, 5 and 7".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Sections 5, 5 and 7 shall survive" is a mechanical error on its face, and the clause also speaks of "expiration" of an MTA that nowhere states a term, so both the survival list and the duration are indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The contract contains two paragraphs numbered 5 (ownership/publication review and the warranty disclaimer) and an unnumbered final paragraph, so the survival list cannot be reconciled with the numbering of the instrument as a whole, and the duty to return "all Materials and progeny" collides with paragraph 3's authorised incorporation of Materials into a clinical-grade vector.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary modification, non-waiver and severability boilerplate whose terms are definite and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carries no paragraph number of its own, so it may read as part of paragraph 10, which matters only marginally given paragraph 10's survival list already misfires; otherwise it conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain administrative instruction on returning the countersigned copy; nothing in it is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the dual signature block and the preamble's request that both the scientist and an authorised institutional official agree, so it fits the instrument.
